response.rationale: C1 is best because it includes the functional pseudo-obstruction mechanism captured by R5 and adds the CT-documented anatomical distribution of both small bowel and colon. R5 is a close runner-up but omits the megacolon/colonic component. Celiac disease is directly contradicted by endoscopy and gluten-free diet failure; lymphangiectasia, alcoholic liver disease, and short bowel syndrome do not explain the surgical exploration showing no mechanical obstruction and the combined small-bowel/colonic dilation.

rejected.why: Celiac disease is disconfirmed by absence of endoscopic evidence and no improvement with a gluten-free diet.
Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency is nonspecific, and intestinal lymphangiectasia does not explain the obstructive pattern and megacolon.
Heavy alcohol use is present but there is no raw evidence of liver-specific dysfunction, and symptoms continued after alcohol cessation.
Short bowel syndrome requires loss of bowel length; only an uncomplicated cholecystectomy is documented and no small-bowel resection is described.
